fr_ancrer_verb.hook: Monsieur Verbe ANCHORS his tiny rowing boat: he drops the little iron ANCHOR into the brook (ahn-KRAY).
fr_ancrer_verb.why: Anchor → ancrer = to anchor; the anchor holds the boat in place.

fr_chuter_verb.hook: Down the hay CHUTE he goes – Monsieur Verbe FALLS, legs in the air (shew-TAY)!
fr_chuter_verb.why: Chute → chuter = to fall, drop; the mime tumbles down the slide.

fr_trotter_verb.hook: Monsieur Verbe TROTS along the path beside a little pony, knees high (troh-TAY).
fr_trotter_verb.why: Trot → trotter = to trot; mime and pony trot together.

fr_prescrire_verb.hook: Doctor Monsieur Verbe PRESCRIBES one nap a day for the yawning sheep (prehs-KREER).
fr_prescrire_verb.why: Prescribe → prescrire = to prescribe; the doctor writes it on his notepad.

fr_synchroniser_verb.hook: Monsieur Verbe SYNCHRONIZES his two alarm clocks so they ring at the same time (san-kroh-nee-ZAY).
fr_synchroniser_verb.why: Synchronize → synchroniser = to synchronize; both clocks show the same time.

fr_refouler_verb.hook: At the fuel pump Monsieur Verbe PUSHES BACK the nozzle: 'No REFUEL today!' (ruh-foo-LAY).
fr_refouler_verb.why: 'Refuel' → refouler = to push back, hold back; the mime refuses the nozzle.

fr_decouler_verb.hook: Monsieur Verbe's DAY-COOLER melts in the sun – the puddle FOLLOWS FROM the melting ice (day-koo-LAY).
fr_decouler_verb.why: 'Day-cooler' → découler (de) = to follow from, stem from; the water comes from the cool box.

fr_flaner_verb.hook: In his FLANNEL scarf, Monsieur Verbe STROLLS slowly past the flowers (flah-NAY).
fr_flaner_verb.why: Flannel / flâneur → flâner = to stroll, wander about.

fr_emaner_verb.hook: A lovely smell EMANATES from the pie on the window sill – Monsieur Verbe follows his nose (ay-mah-NAY).
fr_emaner_verb.why: Emanate → émaner (de) = to emanate, come from; the steam rises from the pie.

fr_rencherir_verb.hook: At the RANCH auction Monsieur Verbe GOES ONE BETTER, raising his paddle with a CHEERY whoop (rahn-shay-REER).
fr_rencherir_verb.why: Ranch + cheery → renchérir = to go further, go one better; he bids again.

fr_handicaper_verb.hook: Monsieur Verbe's horse is the fastest, so it carries sandbags on its saddle – it is HANDICAPPED with extra weight (ahn-dee-kah-PAY).
fr_handicaper_verb.why: Handicap (racing) → handicaper = to handicap, hold back; the extra weight slows the horse.
ex: Ce sac lourd me handicape dans la course.
This heavy bag holds me back in the race.
fr_handicaper_verb.note: Often figurative (to hold back); be kind when talking about disability.

fr_inserer_verb.hook: Monsieur Verbe INSERTS a coin into the vending machine (an-say-RAY).
fr_inserer_verb.why: Insert → insérer = to insert, put in.

fr_actionner_verb.hook: ACTION! Monsieur Verbe WORKS the lever and the little drawbridge creaks down (ahk-syoh-NAY).
fr_actionner_verb.why: Action → actionner = to work, operate (a lever, a machine).

fr_expatrier_verb.hook: Suitcase in hand, Monsieur Verbe sets off past the palm TREE to live abroad – he EXPATRIATES himself, mirror in hand (ehk-spah-tree-YAY).
fr_expatrier_verb.why: Expatriate → s'expatrier = to move abroad, emigrate; the hand mirror shows it is reflexive (s').

fr_parachuter_verb.hook: Monsieur Verbe PARACHUTES down onto the green, landing by the lamp post (pah-rah-shew-TAY).
fr_parachuter_verb.why: Parachute → parachuter = to parachute (in), drop by parachute.

fr_objecter_verb.hook: Monsieur Verbe OBJECTS to his bath: arms braced on the tub's edge, he frowns 'NO!' (ob-zhehk-TAY).
fr_objecter_verb.why: Object → objecter = to object (that); the mime protests.

fr_emigrer_verb.hook: Monsieur Verbe waves goodbye as AMY's GRAY swallows EMIGRATE south (ay-mee-GRAY).
fr_emigrer_verb.why: Emigrate → émigrer = to emigrate, migrate; the swallows leave for the south.

fr_transiter_verb.hook: Riding the package belt, Monsieur Verbe TRANSITS through the sorting shed with the parcels (trahn-zee-TAY).
fr_transiter_verb.why: Transit → transiter = to pass through, transit.

fr_acheminer_verb.hook: Monsieur Verbe's postal pony CONVEYS the package down the lane with A SHIMMY and a happy NEIGH (ah-shuh-mee-NAY).
fr_acheminer_verb.why: 'A shimmy-neigh' → acheminer = to convey, deliver; the pony carries the package along.

fr_vehiculer_verb.hook: Monsieur Verbe's little tow truck TRANSPORTS the broken bicycle – a VEHICLE carrying a vehicle (vay-ee-kew-LAY).
